jobs.title: Chief Development Officer, Alpha - $400,000/year USD
jobs.description:
"the Great Educational Equalizer"

— Philosopher Johnathan Bi, on Alpha School

Alpha is hiring.

You went into private school leadership to shape how children learn, not to run capital campaigns and referee parent committees. There is a version of this job where the academic model is protected for you, operations is handled centrally, and you spend your week on what you are best at: winning over the families who matter most, turning them into advocates, and being the voice of authority when the conversation gets hard.

You will own the parent side of Alpha in one metro — Miami, San Francisco, or Los Angeles. Your measure is enrollment and advocacy: prospective ultra-high-net-worth families who convert, current UHNW families who re-enroll, refer, and publicly champion 2 Hour Learning, and a local community where Alpha is top of mind. Roughly half your week is outward-facing — community partnerships, info sessions, and 1:1 conversations with sophisticated parents who have read every AI skeptic and want to know why the model actually works.

The rest of the seat is the escalation line. When an Associate Dean of Parents reaches the edge of what they can resolve — a board family threatening to pull their kids, a campus quietly softening the model to keep a vocal parent happy — it comes to you. You retain the family, and you keep the model intact. Both. Then you document the precedent so the Associate Dean network can handle it next time without you.

If you have run a private or independent K-12 school, or you have spent a career earning the trust of UHNW families in another industry, and you have been waiting for the job where judgment and persuasion are the actual deliverables, this is it.

What You Will Be Doing

Building local awareness through partnerships with family offices, private clubs, and independent advisors, plus workshops and community events that generate inbound interest
Running admissions for wealthy families end to end: info sessions, 1:1 follow-up in the CRM, and the enrollment decision, including telling a family this is not the right school for their child
Turning enrolled parents into public champions of 2 Hour Learning through advocacy workshops and parent-to-parent networks, so enrolled families become your strongest source of new inquiries
Resolving the escalations others cannot: diagnosing whether the problem is the model, campus execution, or family fit, engaging the family directly, then writing up the precedent for the rest of the network
Keeping current families close through regular touchpoints, and reporting the patterns you hear back to leadership

What You Won’t Be Doing

Capital campaigns, donor cultivation, major gifts, and every other form of fundraising are off your plate entirely
Convening PTAs, School Improvement Councils, parent committees, or focus groups that get a vote on school policy
Managing facilities, finance, legal, vendors, technology, marketing, or community logistics — centralized teams own all of this, so your week stays on relationships, not operations
Designing curriculum or coaching instructional staff on pedagogy; the academic model is owned and protected centrally
Making exceptions or customizations to the educational model to satisfy a parent request, however influential the parent
Simply logging and responding to complaints, or writing newsletters and routine parent communications
Defusing conflict by avoiding it — diplomacy here means delivering hard messages, not softening standards
Working behind the scenes; this is an on-site, full-time, face-of-the-school seat that includes evening and weekend community events

Chief Development Officer Key Responsibilities

Build a metro where Alpha families are 2 Hour Learning’s loudest advocates — and where no parent crisis is resolved by compromising the model.

Basic Requirements

7+ years leading high-stakes relationships in private or independent K-12 education, fundraising or major gifts, enterprise sales, client success, or private wealth management
2+ years working directly and regularly with ultra-high-net-worth or similarly high-expectation families, such as full-pay families at an elite private school, family-office clients, wealth-management clients, or major donors
Proven ownership of measurable enrollment, retention, advocacy, sales, or client outcomes, including resolving sensitive situations and holding firm standards when influential people push back
Polished executive communication, consultative judgment, and genuine conviction in Alpha's accelerated learning model, with the confidence to represent it to skeptical parents and public stakeholders
Living in the Miami, San Francisco, or Los Angeles metro area; authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship; and available for full-time on-site work, including 2 to 4 evening or weekend events per month

Nice-to-have Requirements

Sitting or recent Head of School — or the Head’s right hand — at a top-tier independent K-12 (NAIS-member or peer tier)
Multi-campus or multi-site school leadership experience (regional director, network superintendent, COO of a school network)
A UHNW client-services background translated into school leadership: private wealth management, single-family office, or major-gifts development at an elite prep or Ivy
An existing network among UHNW families or influential local organizations in Miami, San Francisco, or Los Angeles
Crisis communication experience involving press, regulators, or board-level stakeholders
Hands-on AI building experience — custom GPTs, agents, or vibe-coded internal tools used in a real operating context
An advanced degree (M.Ed., MBA, or doctorate) — common in this profile, but not required; no formal education is required for this role

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Job Description

Deputy Managing Director – Operations, LOSSAN Rail Corridor Agency

Under minimal direction, provides executive leadership and oversight of operational, programmatic, and service delivery activities for the LOSSAN (Los Angeles – San Diego – San Luis Obispo) Rail Corridor Agency. This position leads operational integration, service delivery coordination, capital program implementation support, and passenger-focused initiatives supporting the Pacific Surfliner and broader LOSSAN Rail Corridor. Works closely with member agencies, operators, host railroads, regulators, and internal partners to advance safe, reliable, efficient, and customer-focused rail service.

This is an exempt, executive level management position in salary grade 285:

Min – $221,020.80| Mid – $262,579.20 | Max – $304,116.80/annually. The starting salary will be within this range based on qualifications.

This posting will remain open until a candidate is selected.

What You’ll Do

Lead operational and program delivery activities supporting Pacific Surfliner service and the LOSSAN Rail Corridor
Oversee service implementation, operational readiness, performance monitoring, and integrated service delivery
Coordinate operational activities across Operations, Capital Programs, Planning, Finance, Marketing, and passenger-focused initiatives
Lead coordination related to service modifications, disruptions, capital project impacts, and corridor improvements
Partner with host railroads, operators, member agencies, state agencies, regulators, and other stakeholders
Evaluate operational performance, service impacts, implementation risks, and customer experience considerations
Advance corridor resiliency, operational integration, and future rail mobility initiatives
Prepare and present operational updates and recommendations to executive leadership, stakeholders, and the Board of Directors
Represent the Agency in regional, statewide, and national rail and transportation forums
Lead, coach, and develop staff while fostering a collaborative, high-performing environment
Serve as a member of LOSSAN’s executive leadership team and act as backup to the Managing Director, as needed

What We’re Looking For

Bachelor’s degree in business, management, or a related field
Minimum of eight years of senior management experience, including four years of experience managing staff
Experience in transportation, public agency administration, or related transportation operations
Demonstrated ability to lead complex operational and program implementation initiatives
Strong understanding of service delivery, operational performance, and cross-functional coordination
Proven ability to build effective relationships with operators, public agencies, regulators, and other stakeholders
Strong executive-level communication, presentation, decision-making, and problem-solving skills
Ability to translate organizational priorities and Board direction into effective operational strategies
Advanced degree preferred

Why You’ll Love It Here

Help lead one of the nation’s most significant intercity passenger rail corridors
Shape operational strategies that directly influence Pacific Surfliner service and passenger experience
Collaborate with rail operators, host railroads, member agencies, and transportation partners throughout the corridor
Lead complex, high-visibility initiatives that advance rail mobility, reliability, and corridor resiliency
Serve in a key executive leadership role helping shape the future of intercity passenger rail service

Join a team where innovation, integrity, and strategic thinking are valued.

Description

ABOUT LIFEMOVES

LifeMoves is the largest and most effective provider of interim housing and services for homelessness in Silicon Valley since 1987. Our Mission is to end homelessness by providing interim housing, supportive services, and building collaborative partnerships. With over two dozen interim supportive housing communities and more on the way, LifeMoves gives our neighbors experiencing homelessness a temporary place to call home while providing intensive, customized case management through site-based programs and community outreach.

POSITION PURPOSE

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the Senior Director of Institutional Giving leads LifeMoves' institutional fundraising program, with a focus on private, family, and community foundation partners, playing a central role in advancing the organization's $20 million annual fundraising goal. This role carries a personal portfolio of corporate and foundation funders and prospects capable of six- and seven-figure giving, and partners deeply with LifeMoves' Corporate & Community Engagement and volunteer management team to ensure institutional and corporate-partner relationships are aligned and mutually reinforcing.

The ideal candidate is an experienced foundation fundraiser who has personally solicited and closed six- and seven-figure grants, and who brings a stewardship-first mindset to funder relationships — prioritizing deep partnership and long-term trust over one-time asks. This is not an entry-level or first-time management opportunity. LifeMoves is seeking a leader who can inspire, coach, and hold team members accountable, with demonstrated experience managing teams of 2-3 fundraising professionals.

Essential Job Responsibilities

Set and drive LifeMoves' institutional giving strategy, including prospect research, proposal and report development, and multi-year funding pipelines.
Manage and grow a personal portfolio of foundation funders and prospects, personally identifying, cultivating, soliciting, and closing gifts at the six- and seven-figure level.
Lead LifeMoves' foundation relations strategy, including prospect research, proposal and report development, and multi-year funding pipelines.
Partner deeply with LifeMoves' Corporate & Community Engagement and volunteer management team to align institutional funder relationships with corporate partnerships and volunteer engagement opportunities.
Build and lead a high-performing institutional giving team as it grows, coaching staff and holding them accountable to ambitious fundraising goals.
Build deep relationships with Program leadership and leverage their expertise to nurture foundation relationships.
Understand the public funding arena to identify areas for public and private partnerships.
Apply moves-management principles to guide foundation funders through identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
Champion a stewardship-first philosophy in all institutional funder relationships, ensuring funders experience LifeMoves as a trusted partner rather than a transactional grantee.
Collaborate with the Senior Director of Individual Giving and broader Development team to ensure a coordinated, donor-centered fundraising strategy across all funding sources.
Serve as a senior advisor to the CEO and Development leadership on institutional funding trends, risks, and opportunities.
Track and report portfolio and pipeline activity using LifeMoves' Salesforce CRM.
Represent LifeMoves at funder meetings, site tours, and community events, including occasional evenings and weekends.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Education

Bachelor's degree preferred; equivalent combination of education and professional experience will be considered in lieu of a degree.

Qualifications

10+ years of professional development/fundraising experience, with a demonstrated track record of personally soliciting and closing six- and seven-figure gifts from foundations.
Prior foundation fundraising experience required; government grants experience is not required.
Demonstrated success managing, coaching, and developing a team of 2-3 fundraising professionals; proven ability to inspire, coach, and hold team members accountable to ambitious goals — this is not a first-time people-management role.
Working knowledge of moves-management principles and donor-centered fundraising practices.
Genuine commitment to funder stewardship — building long-term, authentic partnerships rather than treating fundraising as transactional.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including strong grant-writing and reporting ability.
Experience with Salesforce CRM systems; ability to use data to inform portfolio and pipeline strategy.
CFRE certification preferred.
Ability to work occasional evenings and weekends and to travel frequently and locally within the Bay Area for funder meetings and events.

COMPETENCIES

Foundation Fundraising & Grant Strategy: Personally identifies, cultivates, solicits, and closes six- and seven-figure foundation gifts, and builds strong, multi-year funding pipelines.
Strategic & Team Leadership: Sets institutional giving strategy and inspires, coaches, and develops staff, setting clear expectations and holding the team accountable to ambitious fundraising goals as the team scales.
Moves Management & Funder Strategy: Applies moves-management discipline to guide foundation funders through identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
Donor/Funder Stewardship: Prioritizes building and nurturing authentic, long-term funder relationships over one-time grants, ensuring funders feel genuinely valued as partners in LifeMoves' mission.
Cross-Team Partnership: Partners closely with the Corporate & Community Engagement/volunteer management team and the Senior Director of Individual Giving to present a coordinated, donor-centered fundraising strategy.
Organizational Leadership: Acts as a senior advisor to the CEO and Development leadership, representing institutional giving perspective in organization-wide planning.

Additional Requirements

Contingent Upon:

Satisfactory results of a background check
Satisfactory results of a DMV Motor Vehicle Record Check
Valid California driver's license, reliable transportation, and current vehicle insurance
Proof of clear TB test dated within 60 days of hire

WORKING CONDITIONS

On-site, in-person working requirements: Hybrid
Supervisory Responsibilities: Currently supervises institutional giving staff, with the expectation of building and managing a team of up to 4-7 fundraising professionals as the department grows.
Travel: Significant travel throughout assigned counties and agency locations on a daily and weekly basis
Physical Demands: Duties may require sitting, standing, walking, climbing stairs, reaching, reading, using computers or other equipment, communicating and exchanging information with others, and lifting or moving up to 25 lbs. LifeMoves provides reasonable accommodations to support performance of essential job functions, as required by law.

Candidates from all backgrounds, including bilingual, bi-cultural, BIPOC, Native and/or Indigenous, LGBTQIA+, and disabled applicants are encouraged to apply. Reasonable accommodation is available for qualified individuals with disabilities during the application process.
